thread.title: Trump Announces Sweeping Tariffs on Imports
thread.title_full: Trump Announces Sweeping Tariffs on Imports

author: The Associated Press
title: Trump Announces Sweeping Tariffs on Imports
text:
• President Donald Trump announced new tariffs on imports during a speech on April 2, 2025.
• Trump stated that the U.S. has been 'looted, pillaged, raped, plundered' by other nations.
• The proposed tariffs include: 34% on imports from China, 20% from the European Union, 25% from South Korea, 24% from Japan, and 32% from Taiwan.
• New Zealand's trade minister, Todd McClay, acknowledged the tariffs on his country's goods and stated they would have an impact on exporters.
• AFL-CIO President Liz Shuler emphasized the need for policies that support U.S. industries and protect jobs alongside tariffs.
• Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent indicated that the tariffs aim to set the stage for long-term economic growth.
• Mexico and Canada are excluded from the tariffs due to a trilateral free trade agreement.
• Economic analyst Gabriela Siller noted that Mexico could gain a competitive edge despite the tariffs.
• Business owners expressed concerns about the impact of tariffs on their operations and pricing.
• The U.S. imports about 80% of its seafood, which will now face higher duties, potentially raising costs and threatening jobs in the seafood industry.
• The tariffs on seafood include 26% on imports from India and 46% from Vietnam.
• The U.S. government plans to close a loophole on small-ticket imported goods from China, removing the 'de minimis' exception for goods valued under $800.
• Trump's tariffs are described as 'reciprocal' and are intended to address perceived unfair trade practices.
• The announcement caused fluctuations in U.S. financial markets, with the S&P 500 showing volatility in trading.
• Trump's speech lasted approximately 45 minutes, during which he predicted that the public would eventually support his economic policies.
